claims.text: AlTiVNb is a lightweight high-entropy alloy system.
The proposed baseline AlTiVNb alloy is near-equimolar and forms a homogeneous solid solution.
Atomic-size mismatch among Al, Ti, V, and Nb generates significant coherent lattice strain.
The lattice strain increases strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Lattice strain modifies diffusion pathways so that an adherent oxide film forms rapidly.
A dense Al2O3/Cr2O3-rich oxide layer can significantly enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The protective oxide film is self-healing.
A continuous passivating oxide layer contributes to corrosion resistance in saline environments.
A minor Cu addition to the proposed lightweight alloy induces elemental segregation.
Cu-induced segregation produces localized variations in lattice strain.
Cu-induced segregation causes discontinuous oxide coverage.
The segregated Cu-modified alloy will have lower yield strength than the homogeneous baseline.
The segregated Cu-modified alloy will have lower ductility than the homogeneous baseline.
The segregated Cu-modified alloy will have a higher oxidation rate at high temperature than the homogeneous baseline.
The segregated Cu-modified alloy will have a higher corrosion current density in saline solution than the homogeneous baseline.
The proposed mechanism should cease to operate at very low oxygen partial pressure because oxide-film formation becomes negligible.
The proposed mechanism should cease to dominate above the solid-solution stability range because phase transformations override lattice-strain and passivation effects.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing a homogeneous AlTiVNb baseline with an otherwise controlled Cu-modified alloy under tensile, 900 °C oxidation, and 0.6 M NaCl corrosion tests.

Statistically indistinguishable mechanical strength, oxidation resistance, and corrosion performance between the segregated and homogeneous alloys would falsify the proposed critical role of homogeneity.
The relative contributions of lattice strain and oxide-film formation are uncertain and may depend on composition and processing.
